CHIEF COMPLAINT
Recurrent kidney stones with recent emergency room visit; follow-up on hypertension and diabetes management.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female presenting with history of recurrent kidney stones. She reports experiencing intermittent pain that prompted an emergency room visit last week. She estimates this is approximately her seventh or eighth kidney stone episode. She believes the current stone passed approximately three days ago. She denies current hematuria and reports resolution of pain. At the emergency room, she was treated with pain medication, specifically Percocet. She has seen a urologist previously, approximately one year ago. She reports home blood pressure readings ranging from 130-140 over 60-70 mmHg, which is improved from initial readings around 180 mmHg. Regarding her diet, she acknowledges difficulty limiting fast food intake due to time constraints but is open to dietary modifications. She reports occasionally experiencing insomnia with worry as a contributing factor and has found meditation apps helpful. She has previously tried melatonin without significant benefit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current chest pain. Denies current abdominal pain. Denies hematuria at present. Denies dysuria. Reports occasional insomnia related to worry; improved with meditation apps. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Recurrent kidney stones (seventh or eighth episode)
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Systolic ejection murmur (grade 2/6, previously known)
Insomnia

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily
Percocet (received at emergency room last week)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports being frequently on-the-go, which contributes to fast food consumption. Reports difficulty with dietary adherence and time management for meal preparation. Uses smartphone regularly, kept at bedside. Prefers sleeping with television on.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles.
Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated; unchanged from previous exams.
Abdomen: Soft, no tenderness to palpation.
Costovertebral angle (CVA): No tenderness bilaterally.
Blood pressure at visit: 150/90 mmHg.

RESULTS
Recent labs reviewed from prior visit: A1C 6.7% (elevated, but improved since initial diabetes diagnosis one year ago).
Urinalysis and urine culture pending.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Recurrent kidney stones: Most recent stone appears to have passed. Will obtain urinalysis and urine culture to ensure resolution. Referral to urology (Dr. Harris) for evaluation and management of recurrent nephrolithiasis to identify underlying etiology.

2. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled on Norvasc 2.5 mg daily. No medication changes needed at this time. Continue current regimen with refills provided via pharmacy. Continue home blood pressure monitoring 2-3 times weekly.

3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Continue Metformin 500 mg daily. Patient to check blood glucose before each meal to better assess dietary impact and glucose control. Referral to nutrition/dietitian to assist with dietary modifications and sodium reduction (goal <2300 mg daily) to support eventual medication reduction.

4. Insomnia: Advised on sleep hygiene practices including turning off electronics, keeping room dark and cool, and utilizing smartphone sleep mode. Recommend trial of Melatonin 10 mg as needed for sleep. Patient declined prescription sleep medications at this time.

Follow-up appointment in 3 months.
